Taras Fliorko

Final-year Robotics Student | Dynamics, Control and Underactuated Systems

I’m a final-year Robotics and Automated Systems student at South East Technological University in Carlow, Ireland. My work brings together mathematical modelling, nonlinear simulation, mechanical design and embedded control. I’m interested in how physical models inform the design and control of robotic systems, particularly underactuated systems. My current final-year project investigates controlled tipping and balance using a single gimbaled reaction wheel. I’m preparing for Master’s study in robotics and control, building on projects in rover manipulation, vision-based navigation and programmable electronics. Contact: tfliorko@gmail.com.

Projects

Gimbaled Reaction Wheel Cube

Simulation and optimisation software for defining the technical specification of a gimbaled reaction wheel cube. Evaluated 19,088 simulated cases across 157 flywheel geometries and developed a weighted design-ranking algorithm.

View Project GitHub

Drone Navigation without GNSS

Co-developed stereo-vision navigation using optical flow, least squares estimation and Kalman filtering. Validated navigation on real data and contributed to drone integration with a team that reached the EUDIS Defence Hackathon Ireland finals.

View Project GitHub

Mars Rover Manipulator

Designed components for a lightweight six-axis rover arm, evaluated structural behaviour through stress simulation, and developed Python control logic for the SETU European Rover Challenge project.

View Project

Smartbreadboard Programmable PCB

Designed a software-configurable breadboard with two MT8816 switch matrices, 256 programmable crosspoints, a custom KiCad PCB and Arduino control firmware.

View Project GitHub

Ball Levitation System

Integrated Arduino sensing with a Siemens PLC over Modbus TCP and tuned PID control in a team-built fan levitation system, maintaining ball height within ±3 mm with a 10-second settling time.

View Project

Technical Notes

Weighted selection of a simulated design

The reaction cube optimiser ranks successful simulation runs using weighted min–max normalisation. The current flywheel routine balances component mass, tipping time and target RPM, then refines candidate parameters around the best tested design. The result depends on the model, tested candidates and selected weights; it is not a claim of a global optimum.

Read more

From programmable crosspoints to circuit routing

Smartbreadboard separates low-level switch control from the longer-term goal of routing complete circuit connections. The current work covers PCB design, Arduino firmware and addressing/control-signal checks. Automatic routing and full electrical characterisation remain development work.
